title: Create the SQS queues
content:
The system uses three Standard SQS queues:
Queue Role Visibility timeout phishing-dlq Dead-letter queue, holds messages that failed processing repeatedly Default phishing-fast-queue Link and email scanning jobs 60 seconds phishing-file-queue File scanning jobs 300 seconds The dead-letter queue must be created first, because the other two queues refer to it.
Visibility timeout When a worker receives a message, SQS hides it from other workers for the visibility timeout. If the worker does not delete the message in that period (because of an error or a timeout), the message becomes visible again and is processed once more. The value must be greater than or equal to the timeout of the Lambda function that consumes the queue. FastDetectWorker has a 45-second timeout and FileDetectWorker has a 90-second timeout (section 5.4.6), so 60 and 300 seconds satisfy this condition.
Create the dead-letter queue phishing-dlq Open Amazon SQS in the AWS Console and select the Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 Region. Choose Create queue. Enter: Type: Standard Name: phishing-dlq Keep the remaining settings and choose Create queue. Create the queue phishing-fast-queue Choose Create queue. Enter: Type: Standard Name: phishing-fast-queue Under Configuration, set Visibility timeout to 1 Minutes (60 seconds). Scroll to Dead-letter queue and choose Enabled: Choose queue: select phishing-dlq Maximum receives: 3 Choose Create queue. Create the queue phishing-file-queue Follow the same steps as above with these differences:
Name: phishing-file-queue Visibility timeout: 5 Minutes (300 seconds) Dead-letter queue: Enabled, select phishing-dlq, Maximum receives 3 How the dead-letter queue works When a message has been received more than Maximum receives times without being deleted, SQS moves it to phishing-dlq. This stops a faulty message from being processed forever.
Only infrastructure-level failures, where the Lambda function ends abnormally, send a message back to the queue. Errors during analysis are caught by the code and stored as a SCAN ERROR result, so they do not put the message in the dead-letter queue.
Result The three queues phishing-dlq, phishing-fast-queue and phishing-file-queue are available in the Singapore Region. Both processing queues point to phishing-dlq with Maximum receives set to 3. Connecting the queues to the Lambda functions is done in section 5.4.6.

title: Create the IAM roles
content:
Each Lambda function uses its own IAM role, granted only the permissions that function needs. As a result, a function that fails or is abused cannot reach the other resources.
Role Used by Permissions needed PhishingIngestLambdaRole IngestLambda Read and write the two DynamoDB tables, send messages to the two queues, create presigned URLs that write to the upload bucket PhishingStatusLambdaRole StatusLambda Read the PhishingScanJobs table PhishingFastWorkerRole FastDetectWorker Receive messages from phishing-fast-queue, update jobs, write the cache PhishingFileWorkerRole FileDetectWorker The same, plus read files from the upload bucket All four roles also get the managed policy AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole so that the function can write logs to CloudWatch.
In the JSON snippets below, replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with your 12-digit AWS account number. The table, queue and bucket names come from sections 5.4.2 to 5.4.4.
How to create a role Do the following for each of the four roles:
Open IAM, choose Roles in the left menu, then choose Create role. Under Trusted entity type choose AWS service, under Use case choose Lambda, then choose Next. Search for and select the policy AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole, then choose Next. Enter the Role name from the table above and choose Create role. Open the new role, choose Add permissions, then Create inline policy. Switch to the JSON tab and paste the matching JSON below. Choose Next, set Policy name to PhishingAccess, and choose Create policy. PhishingIngestLambdaRole { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "ScanTables", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["dynamodb:GetItem", "dynamodb:PutItem"], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:table/PhishingScanJobs", "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:table/PhishingScanCache" ] }, { "Sid": "SendToQueues", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["sqs:GetQueueUrl", "sqs:SendMessage"], "Resource": [ "arn:aws:sqs:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:phishing-fast-queue", "arn:aws:sqs:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:phishing-file-queue" ] }, { "Sid": "PresignedUpload", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::phishing-raw-uploads-<ACCOUNT_ID>/uploads/*" } ] } A presigned URL carries the permissions of the role that created it. This role therefore needs s3:PutObject on the uploads/ prefix. Without it, S3 rejects the browser upload even though the URL is valid.
PhishingStatusLambdaRole { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "ReadJobs", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "dynamodb:GetItem", "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:table/PhishingScanJobs" } ] } PhishingFastWorkerRole { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "ConsumeFastQueue", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["sqs:ReceiveMessage", "sqs:DeleteMessage", "sqs:GetQueueAttributes"], "Resource": "arn:aws:sqs:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:phishing-fast-queue" }, { "Sid": "UpdateJobs", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["dynamodb:GetItem", "dynamodb:UpdateItem"], "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:table/PhishingScanJobs" }, { "Sid": "WriteCache", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "dynamodb:PutItem", "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:table/PhishingScanCache" } ] } PhishingFileWorkerRole { "Version": "2012-10-17", "Statement": [ { "Sid": "ConsumeFileQueue", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["sqs:ReceiveMessage", "sqs:DeleteMessage", "sqs:GetQueueAttributes"], "Resource": "arn:aws:sqs:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:phishing-file-queue" }, { "Sid": "UpdateJobs", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": ["dynamodb:GetItem", "dynamodb:UpdateItem"], "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:table/PhishingScanJobs" }, { "Sid": "WriteCache", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "dynamodb:PutItem", "Resource": "arn:aws:dynamodb:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:table/PhishingScanCache" }, { "Sid": "ReadUploadedFile", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:GetObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::phishing-raw-uploads-<ACCOUNT_ID>/uploads/*" }, { "Sid": "CheckUploadExists", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:ListBucket", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::phishing-raw-uploads-<ACCOUNT_ID>" } ] } The s3:ListBucket permission applies to the bucket itself (no /*). The worker checks whether the file has reached S3 by requesting the object’s metadata. With ListBucket permission and a missing file, S3 returns a 404 error and the worker waits and retries. Without this permission, S3 returns a 403 error and the worker stops immediately with an error, even though the file was uploaded correctly.
Optional permissions for the two workers The two statements below are needed only when the optional features are turned on. Add them to the Statement array of both worker roles.
Writing JSON logs to the reports bucket (when the REPORTS_BUCKET variable is set):
{ "Sid": "WriteAuditLog", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "s3:PutObject", "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::phishing-audit-logs-<ACCOUNT_ID>/logs/*" } Reading API keys from Parameter Store (section 5.4.8):
{ "Sid": "ReadApiKeys", "Effect": "Allow", "Action": "ssm:GetParameter", "Resource": "arn:aws:ssm:ap-southeast-1:<ACCOUNT_ID>:parameter/phishing/*" } Result Four roles exist: PhishingIngestLambdaRole, PhishingStatusLambdaRole, PhishingFastWorkerRole, PhishingFileWorkerRole. Each role has AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole and an inline policy named PhishingAccess. Section 5.4.6 assigns each role to its Lambda function.

title: Clean-up
content:
The resources used in this workshop can keep generating charges if left in place, especially provisioned DynamoDB capacity, S3 data and CloudWatch logs. Once testing is complete, delete them in the order below. The order works from the outer layers inward, which avoids errors caused by resources that are still referenced.
Step 1: Delete API Gateway Open API Gateway and choose the HTTP API of the system. Choose Actions, choose Delete, then confirm. Step 2: Delete the Lambda functions Open Lambda. Select the four functions IngestLambda, StatusLambda, FastDetectWorker and FileDetectWorker. Choose Actions, choose Delete, enter confirm, then confirm. Deleting a function also deletes the event source mappings that connect it to SQS.
Step 3: Delete the SQS queues Open SQS. Select the three queues phishing-fast-queue, phishing-file-queue and phishing-dlq one at a time. Choose Delete, enter delete, then confirm. Step 4: Delete the DynamoDB tables Open DynamoDB and choose Tables. Select the PhishingScanJobs table, choose Delete, then confirm. Repeat for the PhishingScanCache table. Step 5: Delete the S3 buckets A bucket must be empty before it can be deleted.
Open S3 and choose the upload bucket (the RAW_BUCKET value). Choose Empty, enter permanently delete, then confirm. Choose Delete, enter the bucket name, then confirm. Repeat for the reports bucket (the REPORTS_BUCKET value). Step 6: Delete the IAM roles and policies Open IAM and choose Roles. Select the execution roles created in section 5.4.5, then choose Delete. Choose Policies, filter by Customer managed, then delete the policies that were created for the system. Step 7: Delete the Parameter Store parameters Open AWS Systems Manager and choose Parameter Store. Select the parameters with the /phishing/ prefix, choose Delete, then confirm. This step removes the API keys stored in section 5.4.8.
Step 8: Delete the CloudWatch log groups Log groups are not deleted together with the Lambda functions and continue to incur storage charges.
Open CloudWatch, choose Logs, then choose Log groups. Type /aws/lambda/ in the search box. Select the log groups of the four functions above, choose Actions, choose Delete log group(s), then confirm. Final check Open each service above again and confirm that the resource list of the system is empty. The Billing and Cost Management page can be checked the following day to make sure no further charges appear.

title: Create the Lambda functions
content:
The system has four Lambda functions. All use the Python 3.12 runtime and the arm64 architecture. The source code uses only the Python standard library and boto3 (already present on Lambda), so no extra packages are needed.
Function Role (section 5.4.5) Source Memory Timeout IngestLambda PhishingIngestLambdaRole backend\ingest_lambda.py 128 MB 10 seconds StatusLambda PhishingStatusLambdaRole backend\status_lambda.py 128 MB 10 seconds FastDetectWorker PhishingFastWorkerRole detect-workers.zip 512 MB 45 seconds FileDetectWorker PhishingFileWorkerRole detect-workers.zip 1024 MB 90 seconds Create IngestLambda Open Lambda in the AWS Console, select the Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 Region, then choose Create function. Choose Author from scratch and enter: Function name: IngestLambda Runtime: Python 3.12 Architecture: arm64 Expand Change default execution role, choose Use an existing role and select PhishingIngestLambdaRole. Choose Create function. On the Code tab, open lambda_function.py, delete the sample code and paste the full content of backend\ingest_lambda.py. Choose Deploy. Open the Configuration tab, choose General configuration, choose Edit and set Timeout to 10 seconds. Choose Save. Choose Environment variables, choose Edit and add: Key Value JOBS_TABLE PhishingScanJobs CACHE_TABLE PhishingScanCache FAST_QUEUE_NAME phishing-fast-queue FILE_QUEUE_NAME phishing-file-queue RAW_BUCKET phishing-raw-uploads-<ACCOUNT_ID> RAW_BUCKET is required. Without it the system cannot create the presigned URL for files. The other four variables have defaults equal to the values above, but it is better to set them explicitly.
Because the code is pasted into lambda_function.py, keep the default Handler lambda_function.lambda_handler.
Create StatusLambda Follow the same steps as IngestLambda with:
Function name: StatusLambda Execution role: PhishingStatusLambdaRole Code: the content of backend\status_lambda.py, pasted into lambda_function.py, then Deploy Timeout: 10 seconds Environment variables: JOBS_TABLE = PhishingScanJobs Create FastDetectWorker Choose Create function, choose Author from scratch and enter: Function name: FastDetectWorker Runtime: Python 3.12 Architecture: arm64 Existing role: PhishingFastWorkerRole On the Code tab choose Upload from, choose .zip file, select backend\dist\detect-workers.zip built in section 5.4.1, then choose Save. Under Runtime settings choose Edit and set Handler to fast_detect_worker.lambda_handler. Choose Save. Under Configuration → General configuration → Edit, set Memory to 512 MB and Timeout to 45 seconds. Under Configuration → Environment variables, add: Key Value Note JOBS_TABLE PhishingScanJobs Required CACHE_TABLE PhishingScanCache Required REPORTS_BUCKET phishing-audit-logs-<ACCOUNT_ID> Optional, writes JSON logs to S3 VT_API_KEY VirusTotal key Optional GSB_API_KEY Google Safe Browsing key Optional ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY abuse.ch key Optional The API key variables are optional. A source without a key is skipped and the result has lower confidence. The keys can be stored in Parameter Store instead of environment variables (section 5.4.8).
Under Configuration → Triggers, choose Add trigger and enter: Source: SQS SQS queue: phishing-fast-queue Batch size: 1 Choose Add. Create FileDetectWorker Follow the same steps as FastDetectWorker with:
Function name: FileDetectWorker Existing role: PhishingFileWorkerRole Code: the same detect-workers.zip Handler: file_detect_worker.lambda_handler Memory: 1024 MB, Timeout: 90 seconds Ephemeral storage (in General configuration): 1024 MB, because the downloaded file is stored temporarily in /tmp Trigger: SQS phishing-file-queue, Batch size 1 Environment variables for this function:
Key Value Note JOBS_TABLE PhishingScanJobs Required CACHE_TABLE PhishingScanCache Required REPORTS_BUCKET phishing-audit-logs-<ACCOUNT_ID> Optional VT_API_KEY VirusTotal key Optional ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY abuse.ch key Optional VT_UPLOAD_UNKNOWN_FILES true or false Optional, default true When VT_UPLOAD_UNKNOWN_FILES is true, a file that VirusTotal does not know yet is uploaded to VirusTotal for analysis. Set it to false to look up by hash only and never send file content outside.
Batch size and the VirusTotal limit A batch size of 1 means each Lambda invocation processes a single message, which makes debugging easier. The free VirusTotal plan allows 4 requests per minute, so scanning many files in a row can produce HTTP 429 errors. In that case the result has lower confidence instead of failing.
Result Four Lambda functions exist: IngestLambda, StatusLambda, FastDetectWorker, FileDetectWorker. FastDetectWorker is triggered by phishing-fast-queue and FileDetectWorker by phishing-file-queue, both with state Enabled. IngestLambda and StatusLambda are connected to API Gateway in section 5.4.7.

title: Create the API Gateway
content:
The web frontend calls the system through an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API with two routes:
Method Route Lambda function POST /scan IngestLambda GET /scan/{job_id} StatusLambda An HTTP API costs less than a REST API, and the two Lambda functions from section 5.4.6 are written for the HTTP API event format (payload version 2.0).
Create the API and the two routes Open API Gateway in the AWS Console and select the Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 Region.
Under HTTP API, choose Build.
Under Integrations, choose Add integration and enter:
Integration type: Lambda Lambda function: IngestLambda Choose Add integration again and select the function StatusLambda.
Enter API name: PhishingDetectionAPI and choose Next.
Under Configure routes, create two routes:
Method POST, Resource path /scan, Integration target IngestLambda Method GET, Resource path /scan/{job_id}, Integration target StatusLambda Delete the default route ANY /{proxy+} if it is present.
Choose Next. Under Configure stages, keep the $default stage with Auto-deploy turned on, then choose Next.
Choose Create.
When an integration is created in the Console, API Gateway automatically grants itself permission to invoke each Lambda function. No manual permission is needed.
Configure CORS The browser sends a preflight request (OPTIONS) before calling POST /scan with a JSON body. The API must answer this request correctly, otherwise the web frontend reports a CORS error.
Open the new API, choose CORS in the left menu (Develop section), then choose Configure. Enter: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS Access-Control-Allow-Headers: content-type Choose Save. The value * allows any origin to call the API, which is suitable for a workshop. In production, replace it with the specific address of the web frontend.
Rate limiting (optional) Limiting the request rate protects the system and the quotas of the external sources.
Choose Stages in the left menu and select the $default stage. Under Default route throttling, choose Edit. Set Rate to 10 requests per second and Burst to 20, then choose Save. Record the API address Choose API details (or the API overview page) and copy the Invoke URL, which looks like:
https://<api-id>.execute-api.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com This address is used in section 5.4.9 to configure the frontend and in section 5.5 for testing.
Quick check Open PowerShell and replace <INVOKE_URL> with the address you copied:
$base = "<INVOKE_URL>" Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "$base/scan" -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" ` -Body '{"type":"link","payload":"http://paypal-security-update-fake.com/login"}' A correct result is an object with a job_id and a status of PENDING.
Result The API PhishingDetectionAPI has two routes: POST /scan and GET /scan/{job_id}. CORS is configured. The Invoke URL has been recorded. The quick check returns a job_id.

title: Store API keys in Parameter Store (optional)
content:
In section 5.4.6, API keys can be set directly in the Lambda environment variables. A safer alternative is to keep the keys encrypted in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. The keys are stored in one place and both worker functions read them at run time. This section is optional. Skip it if the keys are already set as environment variables or no keys are used.
The code looks up a key in this order: environment variable, then Parameter Store, then it skips that source.
Create the parameters Open Systems Manager in the AWS Console and select the Asia Pacific (Singapore) ap-southeast-1 Region. Choose Parameter Store in the left menu, then choose Create parameter. Enter the details of each parameter from this table: Name Value /phishing/VT_API_KEY VirusTotal key /phishing/GSB_API_KEY Google Safe Browsing key /phishing/ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY abuse.ch key /phishing/VT_BACKUP_API_KEYS Backup VirusTotal keys separated by commas (optional) For each parameter, set Tier to Standard, Type to SecureString, and paste the key into the Value field. Keep KMS key source as My current account with the default key alias/aws/ssm. 4. Choose Create parameter.
Parameter names must match exactly, including upper and lower case. The Standard tier has no storage charge.
Grant read permission The ssm:GetParameter permission on /phishing/* was described in section 5.4.5 under the optional permissions. Add the ReadApiKeys statement to the PhishingAccess inline policy of both PhishingFastWorkerRole and PhishingFileWorkerRole if it is not there yet. The default encryption key alias/aws/ssm needs no extra kms:Decrypt permission. If a customer-managed KMS key is used, that permission must be granted as well.
Configure the two worker functions Do the following for both FastDetectWorker and FileDetectWorker:
Open the function, choose Configuration, then Environment variables and Edit. Add the variable SSM_PREFIX with the value /phishing. Delete the variables that hold keys: VT_API_KEY, GSB_API_KEY, ABUSECH_AUTH_KEY and VT_BACKUP_API_KEYS. Choose Save. Deleting them is required, because the code always prefers environment variables. If an old variable remains, the function will not read the key from Parameter Store.
Operational notes A key read from Parameter Store is remembered for the lifetime of a Lambda execution environment. When a key is changed in Parameter Store, the new value takes effect only when the function starts a new environment. To apply it right away, save the function configuration to force a restart. If a key is missing, the matching source is skipped and the result has lower confidence. The system keeps working. The worker log may show ParameterNotFound for /phishing/VT_BACKUP_API_KEYS when that parameter was not created. This is normal. Result The /phishing/... parameters of type SecureString exist in the Singapore Region. Both workers have SSM_PREFIX set to /phishing and no environment variable that holds a key.

title: Run the web frontend
content:
The Trust Check web frontend is a static page written in HTML, CSS and JavaScript, located in the frontend folder of the source code. In this workshop it runs on the local machine and calls the API created in section 5.4.7.
Configure the API address The API address is declared in the file frontend\js\config.js.
Open frontend\js\config.js in Visual Studio Code. Replace the API_BASE value with the Invoke URL recorded in section 5.4.7, without a trailing /: const CONFIG = { API_BASE: "https://<api-id>.execute-api.ap-southeast-1.amazonaws.com", POLL_INTERVAL_MS: 2000, POLL_MAX_ATTEMPTS: { link: 30, email: 30, file: 45 }, MAX_FILE_MB: 10, MAX_URL_CHARS: 2048, MAX_EMAIL_CHARS: 20000, }; Save the file. This file holds public information only. Never put AWS keys, API keys or passwords in it.
Run the frontend Open PowerShell, change to the frontend folder and start a simple web server:
cd AWS-Phishing-Detection\frontend python -m http.server 8000 Open a browser and go to:
http://localhost:8000/index.html The port must be 8000 and the address must be localhost, because the CORS configuration of the S3 bucket in section 5.4.3 allows only the origin http://localhost:8000. Using another address (for example 127.0.0.1) makes the browser block file uploads.
If the browser still shows an old version of the page, press Ctrl + F5 to reload without the cache.
What the interface provides The interface has three tabs:
Tab Input Limit Link A URL Up to 2048 characters Email The full email content. Paste the headers as well so SPF, DKIM and DMARC can be checked Up to 20,000 characters File A file chosen from the machine Up to 10 MB After submission, the interface asks for the result every 2 seconds until the job completes or the maximum number of attempts is reached.
Result The page http://localhost:8000/index.html opens and shows the three tabs Link, Email and File. API_BASE in config.js points to the Invoke URL of the API that was created. The system is ready for testing in section 5.5.
